hook.speaker: Bhartrihari
hook.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
hook.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
hook.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
hook.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

alternates.speaker: Kausalya
alternates.setting: Holding back tears, Kausalya blesses her son before he leaves for fourteen years in the forest.
alternates.sanskrit: यं पालयसि धर्म त्वं प्रीत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्वामभिरक्षतु॥
alternates.line: May the good you have lived by, gladly and faithfully, now protect you.
alternates.translation: May the goodness you have kept so gladly and so faithfully protect you, tiger of the Raghus.
alternates.misuse: A mother's blessing, not a promise that good people never suffer.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
alternates.sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥
alternates.line: Don't get carried away by good news or crushed by bad. Keep your understanding steady.
alternates.translation: One should not rejoice on getting what is pleasant nor be troubled on getting what is unpleasant. Steady in understanding and undeluded, the knower of Brahman abides in Brahman.
alternates.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
verse.translation: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: Even in success and failure doesn't mean indifferent to them; learn from both without being thrown.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.for_you: You have a plan and the will to follow it. Let your focus be on the work itself. The result will find you in its own time.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verse.sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.
verse.translation: The doer who is free from attachment, does not speak of himself, is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.
verse.why: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

prasang.title: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

verse.meaning: The best kind of doer acts without clinging, without boasting, full of steady resolve and enthusiasm, and remains unchanged by success or failure. This is the sattvic way of acting.
verse.for_you: You are ready to follow the timetable without boasting about it or shrinking back. This steady, quiet effort is the best kind of doing.
verse.try_today: Notice when you want to speak of your own effort, and let the quiet resolve remain.
verse.scene_line: You sit with your books, steady and full of zeal, unmoved by the date on the calendar.

why: steadiness is named as what the best doer carries

verse.speaker: Shiva
verse.setting: Shiva explains to his devotee Bhringi what makes a 'great enjoyer'.
verse.sanskrit: महान्ति सुखदुःखानि यः पयांसीव सागरः । समं समुपगृह्णाति महाभोक्ता स उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Take in big joys and big sorrows the way the ocean takes in rivers: evenly.
verse.translation: One who takes in great joys and sorrows evenly, as the ocean takes in the waters of rivers: that one is called a great enjoyer.
verse.why: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

prasang.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.
prasang.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

verse.for_you: Your timetable is a steady hand. The ocean does not argue with the river; it simply holds it. Let your mind do the same with whatever comes next.
verse.try_today: Notice one river of news arriving today. Let it flow into your wide ocean evenly.
verse.scene_line: You sit with your timetable as the ocean receives the rivers of the world.

why: joy and sorrow taken in alike

verse.setting: Lecture 'Work and Its Secret', Los Angeles, 4 January 1900.
verse.line: pay as much attention to the means of work as to its end.
verse.translation: One of the greatest lessons I have learnt in my life is to pay as much attention to the means of work as to its end. … With the means all right, the end must come.
verse.why: Look after the means; keep the power to let go.

prasang.lesson: Look after the means; keep the power to let go.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: Closing verse of the section praising learning: the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
verse.sanskrit: असन्तो नाभ्यर्थ्याः सुहृदपि न याच्यः कृशधनः प्रिया न्याय्या वृत्तिर्मलिनमसुभङ्गेऽप्यसुकरम् । विपद्युच्चैः स्थेयं पदमनुविधेयं च महतां सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
verse.line: Don't beg favours from the wicked or money from a struggling friend. Stand tall in hard times.
verse.translation: Do not ask the wicked for favours; do not ask a friend of slender means for money; love a just way of earning; do nothing base even when life is at stake; stand tall in trouble; follow in the footsteps of the great. Who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
verse.why: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.
verse.misuse: 'Even when life is at stake' is the poet's intensity; no principle asks you to harm yourself.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

verse.for_you: You have your timetable ready, and you will follow it. That is a just way of earning your future. Stand tall in the months ahead.
verse.scene_line: You sit with your books, and the great ones stand with you in silence.

story.title: In the middle of the hardest day, they stop to water the horses
story.story_hook: Arjuna had until sunset to win or die. At midday he stopped everything to let his horses drink.
story.summary: The sun is moving, his life is forfeit at sunset, and Jayadratha is still miles behind layers of the enemy. Krishna says: the horses are exhausted and wounded, they need water and there is none here.
story.lesson: Those who carry you must be cared for, most of all when there is no time.
story.teaser: Arjuna had until sunset to win or die. At midday he stopped everything to let his horses drink.
